report:
Fresh source assessment of the complete blessing_gate claim, all three ordinary implementation associations, and both complete associated tests. No TODO/N/A entries are present. This refresh ran review start/read/record and source inspection only; root owns test execution, and I make no claim of running the final-source suites.

The required barrier is explicit in CompileTest::run: prepare must return Output before any observation, diagnostic, or query expect-test assertion runs. Its boundary comment explains that only ALL validated, rendered results may reach assertions capable of updating snapshots. prepare validates fixture paths/root/conflicts and edition, parses source directives, checks observation/expectation agreement, materializes the private project, runs independent rustc checking, opens Sage, clears setup events, and invokes collect. Errors and panics during these preparation stages stop the caller before assertions. The final result match accepts only simultaneous Sage and rustc success; a rendered Sage result cannot hide rustc failure, and rustc success cannot hide Sage failure. Omitted diagnostic expectations with emitted diagnostics also fail before comparison.

observe::collect checks the local crate, collects ordinary and accumulated signature diagnostics, verifies marker files belong to the crate, freezes query events, and performs exhaustive Sage matching. It then validates selected observations, rejects invalid/incomplete type rows or invalid symbol correspondence, builds observation strings, projects requested query events and serializes them, and renders diagnostics into an owned Output. All of these operations precede return to run. The current enum-discriminant unsupported diagnostics are produced during check_crate and join the same pre-comparison matching barrier. Query projection and rendering are eager; no deferred output work appears in expectation comparison.

The current rustc adapter separates execute from validate_output: execution failures propagate; output validation rejects non-UTF-8 stderr, unexpected stdout, malformed diagnostics, and abnormal/inconsistent exit status before invoking compiler-aware matching. This refactoring preserves the preparation barrier. Both compiler paths use the matcher in observe.rs, which filters applicable markers, builds severity/location edges, uses augmenting assignment for one-to-one matching, and rejects unmatched markers or diagnostics. The captured parser reads compiler qualifiers from source without mutating source; markers are borrowed immutably downstream. Updating cannot add markers, change conditions, or bypass either compiler's matcher. After successful preparation, run can update all three supplied representation kinds. Its scope is one invocation; there is no global transaction or rollback promise for independent tests or later snapshot I/O.

The complete callsite_updates test visibly prepares a disposable source file and runs it with UPDATE_EXPECT set. A rustc-only warning is introduced while observations are stale; the test requires a Rustc diagnostic mismatch and byte-for-byte unchanged source. This specifically catches the plausible regression of updating Sage observations before accepting the rustc result. It additionally verifies stale comparison fails without updates, a successful updating run inserts the expected literal/type representation, retains the original source marker and empty diagnostic expectation, inserts the observation once, and passes again without updating or further file changes. These are meaningful behavioral assertions, not just associations. The second associated test explicitly documents a structural justification and is a no-op; its pass is not behavioral evidence. The captured RFD permits this structural argument instead of failure injection at every stage. The actual barrier inspected here accounts for fixture, compiler, annotation, observation, matching, projection, and rendering failures for all output kinds. Both test entries and all implementation entries are accounted for. No production change or additional association is required for this anchor, and no unresolved behavioral concern was found. Final refresh after coordinated assertion tightening: inspected the newly captured inputs. The only changed initial source fragment tightens two unselected_private_body_still_reports_errors assertions to require the Sage diagnostic mismatch prefix, excluding rustc-only false positives. Production preparation/comparison code, the blessing claim, both associated test bodies, and association metadata remain unchanged. This strengthens surrounding evidence without introducing a new updating path. Re-captured parser and complete relevant RFD rationale before recording. A subsequent fresh-start diff additionally tightens unresolved_paths_still_require_error_markers to require the Sage prefix. I inspected that sole further change; it likewise strengthens a surrounding assertion without changing the gate or its associated tests. Dependencies were recaptured again for this recording.
